# Buried Signals Benchmarks

> Public benchmarks of tools used in open-source investigation: PDF extraction, browser automation, web scraping, and search. The site also preserves a completed July 2026 OSINT language-model study.

## What this site tells you

Use the reports to compare how tools performed on specific reporting tasks. Each tool case defines a source or fixture, a task, and weighted evidence checks. The harness records commands, outputs, scores, failures, and skipped runs. Scores measure the checks in those cases; they are not a universal ranking of tool quality.

The model study is a fixed historical result, not a rolling leaderboard or a claim about today's models. Check the report date, exact model/version, task, prompt, and scoring method before citing a result.

## Reading a result

- Read the task and expected evidence before comparing its scores.
- Check raw output and whether the tool reached the intended source. Obvious error pages are excluded from scoring.
- Distinguish failed runs from skipped tools with unavailable dependencies, access, or credentials.
- Compare access conditions, versions, settings, runtime, and cost alongside evidence coverage.
- A high score on one document or website does not establish performance on all documents or websites.

- [Tool cases](https://github.com/buriedsignals/benchmarks/tree/main/cases)
- [Model study inputs](https://github.com/buriedsignals/benchmarks/tree/main/data/model-benchmark-2026-07-06)
- [Source and reproduction instructions](https://github.com/buriedsignals/benchmarks)

The website publishes reviewed artifacts. Loading it does not run benchmarks; fresh runs use the repository CLI and require explicit permission for network access or paid providers.
